comments.body:
Confirmed. This is a real orchestration-intent bug, but specifically in initial PR `/orchestrate`, not direct `/fix-pr`.

In the referenced PR #166 comment, the user said:

`@sepo-agent /orchestrate there's a merge conflict to main after merging #162 can you check and fix`

The current code ignores that “fix” intent for PR `/orchestrate`. In [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1232-L1272), initial PR orchestration does this:

- if PR `reviewDecision == CHANGES_REQUESTED`: dispatch `fix-pr`
- otherwise: dispatch `review`

That matches the observed handoff on PR #166: `orchestrate -> review`, reason `manual orchestrate start on PR; dispatching review`.

Direct `/fix-pr` is already routed correctly through [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L721-L741), so I would not change that path.

Proposed fix:

1. Add a small deterministic helper for initial PR `/orchestrate` routing.
2. Keep `CHANGES_REQUESTED -> fix-pr`.
3. Also route to `fix-pr` when the request text explicitly asks to fix the PR, especially merge-conflict language like “merge conflict”, “conflicting”, “rebase”, “resolve conflict”, “fix this PR”.
4. Optionally extend PR status reading to include mergeability/merge-state, so known conflicting PRs route to `fix-pr` even if the wording is less direct.
5. Add tests next to the existing cases in [`orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.ts#L845-L918):
   - `/orchestrate ... merge conflict ... fix` dispatches `fix-pr`
   - plain `/orchestrate` on an open PR without changes requested still dispatches `review`
   - `CHANGES_REQUESTED` behavior remains unchanged
   - direct `/fix-pr` remains one-shot and does not become orchestrated unless launched by orchestrator context

I’d implement this as a narrow routing fix, not by sending PR `/orchestrate` through the planner. The documented architecture says explicit PR `/orchestrate` starts are deterministic, and that pattern is still right here; the deterministic rule just needs to account for explicit fix intent in the request text.

Sepo is dispatching follow-up automation.
